This valuation discount is further validated by a provider key-ratio showing a P/B of 0.65x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.25x [E7]. Fundamental momentum has sharply inflected in the positive direction, evidenced by compounded profit growth surging by 129% over the trailing twelve months [E21], leading to a screen reason for profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E65]. This profit acceleration has sparked an outperformance signal where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 142% as the company starts to beat expectations [E56], alongside rising sales QoQ [E67]. Conceded: the company carries a high trailing P/E of 84.6x [E1], a multi-year trend of declining profits [E19, E20], and a 10-year compounded sales growth rate stuck at just 3% [E14].

Peeti Securities Ltd trades at an exorbitant price-to-earnings ratio of 84.6x according to filed statements [E1], or even higher at 95x against a sector benchmark of just 18.06x [E6]. This lofty multiple is entirely disconnected from the company's stagnant operational reality, evidenced by a miserable 10-year and 5-year compounded sales growth of a mere 3% [E14, E15, E60], which actually devolved into negative 4% over the last 3 years [E16]. Profit metrics are collapsing even faster, highlighted by a compounded profit growth decline of 16% over 10 years, plunging further to negative 42% over 5 years and negative 46% over 3 years [E18, E19, E20]. Furthermore, the business offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4], provides no income return to justify holding its stagnant shares, and sits near the bottom of its 52-week range at just 12% of the way up [E5]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a price-to-book ratio of 0.58x to 0.65x [E2, E7] alongside a recent 129% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21].

Conceded: the company carries a high P/E ratio of 84.6x to 95x against a sector benchmark of 18.06x [E1, E6], exhibits a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], trades near the bottom of its 52-week range at 12% [E5], and has struggled with historical 3-year sales contraction of -4% [E16] alongside long-term profit declines of -16% to -46% [E18, E19, E20]. However, focusing solely on backward-looking multiples ignores the decisive operational inflection currently underway, evidenced by a dramatic 129% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21] that handily triggers a bullish screen for profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E65]. This powerful earnings acceleration has turned profit growth 142% higher than 1-year price growth, signaling that the company is starting to meaningfully outperform expectations [E56]. Furthermore, the market drastically under-appreciates this underlying turnaround by pricing the stock at a steep discount to asset value, with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.58x to 0.65x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.25x [E2, E7]. Finally, recent momentum is further validated by positive sequential sales growth up QoQ [E67] despite past sluggishness, confirming that the deeply discounted market capitalization of ₹ 6.77 Cr [E3] fails to price in the nascent fundamental recovery.

Conceded: [E21], [E65], and [E67]. The bull's reliance on a 129% trailing twelve-month profit growth surge [E21] ignores a catastrophic multi-year structural decline that saw 5-year profits plunge by -42% [E19] and 3-year profits drop by -46% [E20]. This single-year earnings bounce is utterly hollow in the context of stagnant long-term top-line performance, where compounded sales growth has languished at a miserable 3% over both 10-year and 5-year horizons [E14, E15] and contracted by -4% over 3 years [E16]. Furthermore, the bull's claim that a 0.58x to 0.65x price-to-book ratio [E2, E7] represents an unappreciated asset discount is entirely neutralized by a pathetic return on assets (ROA) of just 0.64% compared to a sector benchmark of 1.88% [E8], proving that these low-priced assets generate virtually no economic return. Finally, the narrative of a nascent fundamental recovery collapses against the reality of a year-over-year sales contraction of -1% [E68] and a tiny micro-cap valuation of ₹ 6.77 Cr [E3] that is fully justified by an exorbitant P/E ratio of 84.6x to 95x versus a sector benchmark of 18.06x [E1, E6].
